title: Reading Text Files with getline
learningObjectives: Use std::getline to read an entire line, including spaces.
Explain how getline handles the delimiter and removes it from the resulting string.
Mix line-based and token-based input safely by clearing leftover newline characters.
Validate parsed text and report malformed input.
Handle empty lines, final lines without a trailing newline, and read failures.

understand.concept: std::getline reads characters from an input stream into a std::string until it reaches a delimiter (newline by default). The delimiter is consumed but not stored, so spaces inside a line remain. Its return value is the stream, allowing the read to be used as a loop condition.
understand.whyItMatters: Line-based input is useful for names, sentences, CSV-like records and text files where whitespace is meaningful. Reading with operator>> stops at whitespace, so it is not interchangeable with getline.
understand.explain: Include <string> and use std::getline(input, text). It returns the stream, whose state determines whether the read succeeded. A final line without a newline is still read. Empty lines produce an empty string but are successful reads. When switching from formatted extraction such as cin >> number to getline(cin, text), consume the remaining newline first with std::getline(cin, leftover) or use a carefully chosen ignore() call. Validate each record before trusting its fields.

examples.title: Read a line from a text file
examples.explanation: getline keeps spaces in each line. It removes the newline delimiter, then the program adds its own newline for display.

examples.title: Read a full sentence from the keyboard
examples.explanation: Unlike cin >> sentence, getline reads until Enter and preserves internal spaces.

examples.title: Handle formatted input followed by a line
examples.explanation: Formatted extraction leaves the Enter newline behind. ignore() consumes through that newline so getline can read the next complete line.

examples.title: Parse a line and validate the numeric field
examples.explanation: Read the entire record as a line, then use a string stream to parse fields. Check the extraction result before using the values.

examples.title: Treat an empty line as valid input
examples.explanation: An empty line is different from a failed read: getline succeeds and stores an empty string when the user presses Enter immediately.

practise.guidedTask: Read a sample text file containing three lines, including one line with spaces and one blank line. Print each line with its line number. Then test a missing file and explain how the loop terminates.
practise.independentTask: Build a simple contact-record reader. Use getline to capture each complete line, parse the name and age with istringstream, validate the age, and skip or report malformed records. Test blank lines, names with spaces, invalid numbers and a final line without a newline.
hints: getline reads through the delimiter but does not place that delimiter in the string.
Use the returned stream state as the loop condition.
When switching from cin >> value to getline, remove the leftover newline.
A blank line can be a successful read; check both read success and line.empty().
Parse into temporary values and validate before using them.

questions.prompt: What does std::getline(input, text) normally read up to?
options: The newline delimiter (consumed but not stored)
The end of the entire program
questions.explanation: The default delimiter is newline; getline consumes it without storing it in the string.

questions.prompt: Why is getline useful for reading a person's full name?
options: It preserves spaces within the line
questions.explanation: getline reads the whole line, so names such as 'Mary Jane' are retained.

questions.prompt: After cin >> age, why might the next getline read an empty string immediately?
options: The stream is always closed after >>
The newline left in the input buffer is consumed by getline
age was declared as an integer
questions.explanation: Formatted extraction leaves the Enter newline in the input buffer; consume it before the next line read.

questions.prompt: Which condition distinguishes a successful blank-line read from a failed read?
options: The getline return stream state, then line.empty()
questions.explanation: An empty string can be a valid line. First check whether getline succeeded, then decide how to handle empty content.

questions.prompt: How should a program handle a line containing a numeric field that cannot be parsed?
options: Assume it is zero without checking
Check extraction success and report or reject the record
questions.explanation: Validate extraction and the resulting value before using it; malformed records should be handled explicitly.
